answers.answer:
Quick status, then one thing to do.

The leak itself is done and holding. The fix — every fetch wrapped in `async with session.get(...)`, so responses get released on any branch — is deployed to staging and the overnight soak came back flat in memory. So the original 400MB-to-6GB climb is gone; the fix looks real.

But the hunt left an aftereffect: p99 on staging is up about 30% since the fix. Memory flat, latency bent. And the likely cause, from what we walked through, is the retry path — it builds its own ClientSession per retry instead of reusing one, so retries pay a fresh DNS/TLS handshake. That also explains why p99 rose first: retries are the slow tail.

So your next step is the one you parked on Friday: reuse one shared ClientSession in the retry path[k56]. That's the fix. Then the test we agreed on — flat memory with p99 back down means clean; if p99 holds, we're back to the connector-pool explanation[k60].

One caution before you call it done: while we were tracing this, we noticed the retry path might not be the only place building its own session[k59]. Worth a quick look across the other call sites too, so you're not chasing the same problem twice.

And hold off on the ship-to-prod, 10-hour soak[k43] until this is in — right now that soak would be measuring the unfixed retry path plus any other un-reused sessions, so the curve could bend for reasons the leak fix didn't cause[k66].
